cards.title: How does the keyword match work?
cards.body: The feature says the search box filters by title and description in real time. What does one query mean when it runs against an item? Facts: items are plain strings on the client (`feedItems`), a preset feed is uncapped and a custom feed is capped at 100 items, so matching happens over at most a few hundred items per feed.

options.text: Case-insensitive substring; a query with several words requires ALL of them to appear (AND)
Case-insensitive substring; a query with several words matches when ANY word appears (OR)
The whole query is one phrase — exact case-insensitive substring, word boundaries ignored
Case-sensitive exact substring

rec.why: Case-insensitive AND matches what users expect from 'keyword search' (narrowing as they type more words), is trivially testable, and needs no tokenization beyond splitting on whitespace.

cards.title: Match against raw description markup or visible text?
cards.body:
Fact: `item.description` is HTML — the template renders it with `[innerHTML]`, so descriptions carry tags and entities (e.g. `

`, `ä`). Matching the raw string can hit matches inside markup (`query "div"` matching every item with a `

`) and miss text hidden behind entities.

options.text: Strip tags and decode entities first; match only the visible text of the description
Match the raw description string including markup

rec.why: Users think in visible words, not markup; raw matching produces false positives on tag names and false negatives through entities. Stripping is a pure function, so an outcome-based test can fail on it.

cards.title: Are umlauts folded when matching?
cards.body: The feeds are German police reports, so titles and descriptions contain ä/ö/ü/ß. Should a query typed without diacritics still match (e.g. 'schaden' matching 'Schäden'), or must the query use the exact letters as written?

options.text: No folding — matching is plain case-insensitive; the query must contain the letters as written
Fold diacritics on both sides (ä=a, ö=o, ü=u, ß=ss) so 'schaden' matches 'Schäden'

rec.why: Keep the smallest correct change: users searching German reports type the umlauts anyway, and folding rules (ä→a vs ä→ae) are a rabbit hole that belongs to a follow-up if wanted.

cards.title: What shows when the query matches zero items?
cards.body: Today the list area shows either items or the generic 'No feed items loaded' empty state, which is driven by `feedItems.length`. With an active query that filters everything out, the visitor needs to tell 'feed empty' apart from 'nothing matches your filter'.

options.text: A distinct message like 'No items match your search.' shown only while a query is active
Reuse the existing generic empty-state block
Show nothing — just an empty list

rec.why: Conflating 'no matches' with 'no feed loaded' is actively misleading; a distinct message is one observable outcome a test can fail.

cards.title: What does the item count show while filtering?
cards.body: Fact: the feed-info header prints `{{ feedItems.length }} item(s)`. Under an active filter the displayed list is shorter than the loaded list, so that number would silently lie about what is on screen.

options.text: While a query is active, show 'X of Y item(s)'; with an empty query keep 'Y item(s)' unchanged
Always show only the currently displayed count
Leave the header showing the total regardless of filtering

rec.why: 'X of Y' states both facts with no ambiguity and leaves the no-filter rendering byte-identical to today; B hides how much the filter is hiding, C shows a count that contradicts the visible list.

cards.title: What happens to an open item detail while filtering?
cards.body: Fact: `selectedIndex` is an index into the full `feedItems` array and drives the expanded AI-analysis detail. Filtering hides list entries but keeps the underlying array and its indices intact, so an open detail can either persist or be closed when the query changes.

options.text: Collapse the open detail whenever the query changes, and again on every new feed load
Keep the detail open as long as its item still matches the query; collapse it only when the query filters that item out

rec.why: The index stays valid because filtering is a subset of the same array, so persistence costs almost nothing; A closes a report the visitor is reading (possibly mid-AI-analysis) just for typing one more character, and a filtered-out detail lingering open is confusing.

cards.title: Is the query cleared when a feed loads?
cards.body: Two load paths exist: 'Load Selected Feed' (new feed or pasted custom URL) and Refresh (reloads the currently loaded feed, per the glossary). Should the search box carry its query across a load or start clean?

options.text: Clear the query and the filter on every load — Load Selected Feed and Refresh alike
Clear only on 'Load Selected Feed'; Refresh keeps the query and re-applies it to the reloaded items
Never clear — the query always survives loads

rec.why: A stale filter over freshly loaded items is the classic 'why is my list empty' bug; starting clean after any load is one predictable rule that matches the glossary's idea that Refresh re-displays the feed as it is.

cards.title: Where does the search box sit and when is it visible?
cards.body: The page has a feed-selection row (dropdown, Refresh, custom URL, Load button) and a feed-info header that appears once items are loaded. Filtering only means anything while a feed is loaded, but the box could still live in either place.

options.text: In the feed-info header area, shown only while a feed with items is loaded
In the feed-selection input row, always visible but disabled until items are loaded

rec.why: It keeps the feature scoped to the 'currently loaded feed' the sentence names, avoids a permanently disabled control in the selection row, and leaves the existing form and its tests untouched.

cards.title: Does the search box need a clear control?
cards.body: Beyond deleting the text by keyboard, a small clear affordance resets the filter in one action.

options.text: Plain input only — visitors clear by deleting the text
A clear (×) button inside the box, visible only while the query is non-empty

rec.why: Minimal scope for one sentence of feature; a clear button is nice-to-have and can arrive as a follow-up without changing any settled behavior.

cards.title: Confirm shared understanding
cards.body: Settled so far: a client-side, real-time keyword search box over the currently loaded feed's items matching title and description. If you accept the recommendations above (case-insensitive AND substrings over visible text with no diacritic folding; distinct no-match message; 'X of Y item(s)' while filtering; detail open while its item still matches; query cleared on every load; box in the feed-info header with no clear button), the design tree is complete and the next step is /to-spec. Confirm, or answer the cards differently and a new round follows.

options.text: Confirmed — shared understanding reached, proceed to the Spec
Not confirmed — my answers above change the picture; ask another round

rec.why: With the nine cards above answered, no branch of the design tree is left silently assumed; anything further (tests, wording) is Spec detail, not grill material.
